name: Linden Room
note: Nightbird site places the bar at 292 Linden St, next to Nightbird at 330 Gough St.

facts.text: A craft cocktail bar run by the team behind Nightbird, chef Kim Alter's restaurant.
Seating is first come, first served for cocktails, in a small space.
Has two full bars and two levels of lounge seating.
Carries on Chinatown's live music nightclub tradition, with live bands followed by a DJ.
A craft beer, wine and cider tap room and bottle shop, open since 2014.
Has no kitchen, and guests may bring their own food.

name: Liverpool Lil's
note: SFist (2016) title says Liverpool Lil's closed for good after a fire; Yelp lists it as closed at 2942 Lyon St.

facts.text: Sits in the former Examiner printing room in the basement of the Hearst Building.
Decor draws on 1950s and 1960s newspaper offices, with vintage paper presses.
A sports bar and grill near Oracle Park with more than a dozen TVs.
Has more than 20 beers on draft.
The building was a grocery store, possibly built in 1895.
Jane Seabrook and Mark Green bought the bar in 1991 and planted the palm tree out front.
Danny Boyle ran the bar as Ireland's 32 from 1962 to 1982.
Opened in 1989 at Howard and 7th, and was demolished after the Loma Prieta earthquake.
Rebuilt at its current Harrison Street spot, where the bear scene merged with the biker crowd.
Founded by Rick Redewill.
Hosts Jock Sundays, a weekly party that benefits a different LGBT sports team each week.
Its cocktail program is themed on San Francisco landmarks and destinations.
Pairs cocktails with comfort bar food.
Opened in 2022 in Lower Nob Hill as a cocktail bar and restaurant.
Makes handmade cocktails with contemporary techniques and fresh ingredients.
A brewpub that makes its own beers and Spice Girls-inspired cocktails.
Decorated with a sea creature theme.

name: Lucita Niteclub
note: Lucita's Nightclub at 3247 Mission St (at 29th) confirmed by LocalWiki; no single-source facts.

facts.text: A live music bar with weekly bluegrass, blues and jazz jams.
The bar is built from reclaimed wood from a 150-year-old farmhouse.
Has a fireplace against an exposed brick wall and sliding front windows.
A cocktail lounge focused on handcrafted drinks and seasonal ingredients.
The space was once a leftist HQ and printing press, a Prohibition speakeasy and a pirate radio station.
